PullRequest.Title: Dictation: download Foundry Local native runtime on demand
PullRequest.Body:
Re-applies #326678 (on-device dictation via Foundry Local streaming ASR) **without shipping its native payload**, so we keep VS Code's minimum supported Linux glibc floor (Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10 / RHEL 8).

## Problem
#326678 bundled `foundry-local-sdk`'s prebuilt N-API addon (`foundry_local_napi.node`) and native core libraries. The addon requires `GLIBC_2.34` (verified on both `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` via `.gnu.version_r`). The Linux dependency generator scans every shipped `.node` and would declare `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, raising the floor for the **entire product** and dropping Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10-11 / RHEL 8. It was reverted in #326769.

The ONNX Runtime / Foundry Core `.so` libraries themselves satisfy the current floor — only the addon is the problem.

## Approach — download the native runtime on demand
Rather than raise the whole-product glibc floor for an experimental feature, the native runtime is downloaded on demand at runtime, only on supported platforms, into a per-user writable cache. The GLIBC_2.34 addon is never in the scanned/declared package, so the floor is intact.

- **Packaging (`build/`)** — exclude every `foundry-local-sdk/prebuilds/**` and `foundry-local-core/**` from the package; drop the build-time core fetch (`ensureFoundryLocalCorePackage` / `build/lib/foundryLocal.ts`), the Linux dep-generator soname additions, and the darwin universal/macho skip entries.
- **SDK loader patch (`build/npm/postinstall.ts`)** — patch the SDK's `dist/detail/coreInterop.js` to honor `VSCODE_FOUNDRY_LOCAL_NATIVE_DIR` for both addon and core-library resolution, falling back to the original package-relative logic so dev-from-source still works. Idempotent; warns (does not fail) if the SDK's loader shape changes.
- **Runtime downloader (`src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/foundryLocalRuntime.ts`)** — before loading the SDK, ensure the addon (extracted from the pinned `foundry-local-sdk` npm tarball) and the core libraries (via the SDK's own NuGet installer `runInstall`, targeted at the cache with its `binDir` option) are present, then point the loader at the cache via the env var. Version-stamped by SDK version, idempotent (`.complete` marker), and de-duped across concurrent sessions.

Cache layout mirrors the SDK package layout so the loader patch is a trivial path join:

```
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/prebuilds/<rid>/foundry_local_napi.node
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/foundry-local-core/<rid>/<core libs>
```

The **model** itself continues to download on demand at first use (unchanged).

## Proxy support
All three provisioning download legs honor a configured proxy:
- The npm-registry addon tarball (our own fetch) and the NuGet core libraries (via the SDK's bundled installer) read the standard proxy environment variables (`HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`, with `NO_PROXY`) — our fetch attaches an `HttpsProxyAgent`, and the SDK's bare `https.get` calls are routed by temporarily pointing `https.globalAgent` at it (restored afterwards, no SDK patching). This matches how the GitHub desktop app's Rust `foundry-local-sdk` (reqwest/ureq) reaches the same endpoints.
- VS Code's `http.proxy` / `http.noProxy` **settings** are bridged into the dictation utility process and applied as those same environment variables before any download, so a proxy configured only in VS Code (not in the OS environment) is honored — including by the native Foundry Local **model** download, which reads OS-level/env proxy the same way.
- `http.proxyAuthorization` (a `Basic <base64>` value) is folded into the proxy URL's credentials, so both our fetches and the native model download authenticate to the proxy. `http.proxyStrictSSL: false` disables TLS certificate verification for the Node download legs (scoped to the dedicated dictation utility process).

TLS-intercepting proxies otherwise rely on the CA certificate being present in the OS trust store (matching `@vscode/proxy-agent` and the desktop app). Non-`Basic` proxy auth schemes (e.g. Negotiate/NTLM), and disabling TLS verification for the native model leg, are left to OS-level configuration.

## Also in this PR
Un-reverting #326678 also restores these related changes it originally made:
- Removes the `@huggingface/transformers` dependency and deletes the `build/npm/stubs/sharp/` stub it required.
- Deletes the prior on-device transcriber path (`nemotronTranscriber.ts`, ~797 lines), superseded by Foundry Local streaming ASR.
- Bumps `tar` `^7.5.16` → `^7.5.20`, kept in sync with the root `package.json` / lockfile for the hygiene check.

## Supported platforms
-  `darwin-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win32-x64`, `win32-arm64` (mirrors the SDK RID map and the existing dictation gate).

Un-reverts #326678. Refs #326769.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The old path, payload magnitude, deleted reader, unchanged root, and incompatible new model ID are explicit. Only adoption of the experimental feature is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: persistent model files and disk bytes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each legacy model already cached under chatDictationModels remains in addition to the new Foundry model; the deleted transcriber documents the prior default payload as approximately 800 MB.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: retained disk usage and disk-space pressure after upgrade
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Legacy Nemotron and Whisper files in chatDictationModels were the active reusable cache.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The PR deletes the legacy cache consumers and switches model IDs, then points the new Foundry manager at the same cache root without retiring legacy files.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 474 makes the new Foundry manager populate the existing dictation cache while this diff deletes the only legacy-cache consumer and changes the model identity, turning previously reusable model bytes into permanent dead cache data.
Findings.Title: Clean up the superseded dictation model cache
Findings.Impact: Existing dictation users retain the old approximately 800 MB default model and must also store the new Foundry model; the unreachable old payload persists across sessions and upgrades.
Findings.Evidence: Deleted `NemotronTranscriber.prepare` placed the prior model under `chatDictationModels/nemotron/<model@revision>` and documents an approximately 800 MB download. The diff deletes that reader, migrates legacy IDs to a new Foundry ID, and added line 474 configures the new manager with the unchanged cache root. No cleanup or remaining reader exists in the repository.
Findings.Recommendation: After the Foundry model is successfully available, remove the known legacy Nemotron and transformers cache layouts with a one-time, version-aware cleanup that does not race older running windows.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The per-window worker ownership, process-local deduplication, shared cache path, and download-before-promotion ordering are all explicit in the changed code. Only the exact payload size and frequency of simultaneous first use are uncertain, which affects severity rather than the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: network bytes, temporary disk bytes, and four download operations per utility process (one npm tarball plus three NuGet artifacts)
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold cache, work scales linearly with the number of VS Code windows that start dictation before any one process publishes the completion marker; each window owns a separate utility process and therefore a separate process-local inFlight map.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: duplicate large native-runtime downloads contend for bandwidth and disk I/O, increasing first-use latency and transient disk usage
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The native transcription runtime was bundled with VS Code, so starting dictation did not provision an npm addon tarball or three NuGet native packages at runtime.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each window's utility process observes the same cold shared cache, creates its own process-unique staging directory, and downloads the complete runtime before attempting atomic promotion; the inFlight map only deduplicates callers inside one process.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 133 creates a process-specific staging directory for the newly added runtime provisioning path; combined with the added process-local `inFlight` map and the download calls immediately below it, this makes concurrent cold-cache utility processes independently fetch the same payload. Before this diff those runtime network boundaries did not exist.
Findings.Title: Coalesce runtime provisioning across VS Code windows
Findings.Impact: With multiple VS Code windows open, starting first-use dictation in a second window while the first is still preparing launches a second full runtime provision. The loser only discovers the winner after both the npm tarball and all three NuGet artifacts have downloaded, causing avoidable bandwidth/disk contention and slower preparation.
Findings.Evidence: `LocalTranscriptionService` is instantiated inside a per-window utility worker. `ensureFoundryLocalRuntime` checks the shared marker, but its `inFlight` map is module/process-local. `doEnsure` then calls `ensureAddon` and `ensureCoreLibraries` before `promoteDir`; `ensureCoreLibraries` requests three native artifacts. The process-unique staging path at line 133 explicitly permits every process to perform all downloads, and atomic rename only prevents corrupt publication, not duplicated transfer.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a cache-root filesystem claim/lock so one process provisions while others wait for and re-check the completion marker; include stale-lock recovery and preserve the existing atomic staging/promotion semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: First on-device dictation on a cold runtime and model cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The renderer lazily creates a per-window utility process and sends start. Audio capture starts immediately, but the first transcript requires native-runtime provisioning, SDK/manager initialization, model download/load, and session.start; stop also awaits the open promise. Runtime and model downloads therefore gate useful transcription even though microphone capture proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the local-transcription utility worker and invoke start/getModelStatus
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker creation per workbench window on first use, then one start and one status snapshot per dictation session
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lazy utility-process and IPC service shape existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Worker creation and start must complete before renderer capture setup; status reporting follows start.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check completion marker, addon, and three required core libraries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five synchronous existence checks per runtime ensure; normally once per utility process/model load
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No separate native-runtime cache existed or was checked.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These checks decide whether network provisioning is required and are on the model-open path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the pinned foundry-local-sdk npm tarball to extract one native addon
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One tarball per cold-cache provisioning process; redirects are bounded to five
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The native addon was bundled; no runtime npm download occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before SDK import and transcription session creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install Foundry Core, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime GenAI NuGet artifacts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runInstall call containing three artifacts per cold-cache provisioning process; SDK-internal request concurrency is not visible here
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ONNX native runtime was bundled; these three runtime package downloads did not occur.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete after addon fetch and before SDK import/model preparation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write temporary tarball/extraction, process-specific staging payload, atomic promotion, and completion marker
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary addon tree and one staging runtime tree per provisioning process
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No first-use runtime extraction or cache publication occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Promotion and verification must finish before SDK loading.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the selected Foundry Local model through model.download
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical model download on a cold model cache; internal file request count is owned by the SDK and not visible
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior implementation also downloaded the selected on-device model on first use, from Hugging Face rather than Foundry Local.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before model.load and live session creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective runtime-download cardinality is the number of workbench windows entering first use before any process publishes the shared marker. Within one utility process calls coalesce by override directory; across windows they do not. Payload work is one npm tarball plus three NuGet artifacts per racing process.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Addon and core provisioning are serialized within one process. The inFlight map coalesces same-process callers, but every window owns a separate utility process and can provision concurrently without a cross-process lock; each uses a unique staging directory and only converges at final rename.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm runtime cache verifies marker and payload then performs no network work. Cold successful provisioning writes a per-platform marker. Failures leave no positive marker and retry on the next attempt; same-process attempts coalesce only while in flight. Model caching is delegated to Foundry Local.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: worker ownership, cache key, process-local map, download order, and publish point are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact compressed/native payload size and frequency of users invoking dictation in multiple windows during the same cold interval are unknown; the duplicated request count and critical-path placement are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable concurrency burst: racing windows independently download all four runtime artifacts before loser detection.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm-cache dictation and live audio streaming
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the cached model is loaded and session.start completes, each 4096-sample audio callback crosses IPC and is appended to native core through one FIFO chain; native streaming results cross IPC and update the editor. stop waits for queued appends, native stop, and stream drain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send PCM16 audio chunks to the utility process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per 4096 samples, approximately 3.9 calls/second at 16 kHz
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The renderer already sent the same capture chunks over the local transcription proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each chunk must be appended in order for transcription; calls are asynchronous from the audio callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append each audio chunk to the native live transcription session
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately 3.9 serialized native append calls/second while recording
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old utility service retained chunks and periodically ran local ONNX inference instead of making a native streaming append per chunk.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Live recognition consumes the FIFO; stop waits for the tail before native session.stop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit cumulative transcript results to the renderer and replace/decorate editor text
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One renderer event per Foundry stream result; result frequency is SDK/model controlled
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old implementation emitted debounced interim results about every 1.2 seconds; the exact new native result rate is not established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the live rendering path; each event updates editor text and restarts one 700 ms timer.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Recording duration controls audio IPC/native append count linearly; endpointed segment count controls transcript accumulation. The capture callback rate is fixed at about 3.9/second.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Native appends are explicitly serialized by one promise chain; result consumption is one async iterator. Renderer audio callbacks can have outstanding IPC promises but no aggregate concurrency issue is proven at the fixed callback rate.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The loaded model promise/model/manager are retained and reused within the window utility process. A warm disk cache avoids runtime/model downloads but each new window loads its own native model into memory.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for IPC cardinality and serialization; insufficient evidence that native result frequency or append latency exceeds real-time capacity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Foundry result emission frequency and native append duration are not measurable from repository code, so no high-confidence live-render or append-backlog regression is reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression: work scales linearly at a low fixed audio callback rate and has explicit ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Upgrade after using a legacy Nemotron or Whisper dictation model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On first dictation after upgrade, configuration migration selects the new Foundry model. Runtime provisioning and the new model download/load proceed from the existing chatDictationModels root; old model files are not consulted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain legacy Hugging Face/Nemotron model files while writing the new Foundry model cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stale payload for each legacy model the user previously cached; the prior default alone is documented as approximately 800 MB
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Those files were the active reusable model cache for the prior transcriber.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Legacy bytes are off the transcription critical path but permanently consume disk alongside the required new model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download the incompatible new Foundry model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical cold download after migration
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A user with the prior default cached did not need another model download for subsequent sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks first transcript/session opening; old cached model bytes cannot satisfy it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Retained bytes scale with the count and size of legacy model variants previously used; the common prior default contributes about 800 MB.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One model promise coalesces within a utility process; cross-window SDK behavior is not visible. Retention itself has no concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The cache root is unchanged but the model ID/runtime and layout are replaced. No remaining reader or cleanup exists for the old nemotron subtree or transformers cache, so legacy positive cache entries become permanent dead data.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: old path/layout, deleted reader, new model identity, and unchanged cache root are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of users who exercised the experimental feature and whether they cached multiple model choices are unknown; per-affected-user stale payload size for the prior default is documented in deleted code.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: substantial previously reusable model data becomes permanently unreachable without cleanup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel dictation while first-use preparation is still running
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cancel stops capture and increments the session generation, but runtime provisioning uses CancellationToken.None and model preparation remains in flight. This work is no longer on the canceled UI path but can continue to populate reusable caches.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Continue native runtime and model downloads after the initiating recording is canceled
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight runtime provision and one model preparation per utility process/model selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old model preparation also continued after cancel, though it had no separate runtime provisioning leg.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the canceled interaction's critical path; consumes background network/disk and may warm later use.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Bounded by one preparation promise per model in the utility process rather than by repeated audio events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-process provisioning/model work is coalesced. Cancel invalidates the session generation but does not cancel the download.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful background completion leaves reusable runtime/model cache entries; failures clear the model promise and can retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for non-cancellation, lower for harmful impact because the behavior is bounded and intentionally warms the cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: How often users cancel during initial preparation is unknown, and the work has future cache value.
Scenarios.Verdict: Not separately reported: model preparation already continued after cancel before the diff, and the added bounded runtime leg does not independently establish a high-confidence material regression beyond the reported provisioning issue.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 18 changed files. Two concrete regressions were submitted: duplicate cross-window cold runtime provisioning and retention of superseded legacy model caches. Build packaging, warm streaming, cancellation, transcript rendering, IPC cardinality, cache hit/miss behavior, and native-session cleanup were also traced; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
